CFML Language Reference: Functions

DollarFormat

Returns a number as a dollar string: a dollar sign, thousands separators and two decimal places. Negative amounts are wrapped in parentheses, the way accountants like them.

Category

Display and formatting functions

Syntax

DollarFormat(number)

Parameters

number
The amount to format. An empty string is treated as zero.

Returns

A string such as "$1,234.50" or "($1,234.50)".

Usage

The result is always in U.S. dollars, whatever the current locale. To format money the way the current locale expects, use LSCurrencyFormat; for euro amounts, LSEuroCurrencyFormat.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFQUERY NAME="GetPay" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets" MAXROWS="5">
SELECT FirstName, LastName, Salary FROM Employees ORDER BY LastName
</CFQUERY>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Employee</TH><TH>Salary</TH><TH>Above (below) $50,000</TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="GetPay">
<TR><TD>#FirstName# #LastName#</TD>
    <TD ALIGN="right">#DollarFormat(Salary)#</TD>
    <TD ALIGN="right">#DollarFormat(Salary - 50000)#</TD></TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
